expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes ("""), none use ''' or single-line ' quotes
expectations.evidence: Every docstring opens/closes with """ (lines 1, 22, 43, 62, 89, 106, 135); no ''' or single-quote docstrings anywhere.

expectations.text: Module, class, and every public method have a docstring; multi-line docstrings have a one-sentence first line ending with a period, then a blank line
expectations.evidence: All seven docstrings present; each first line is one sentence ending in a period with a blank line after, e.g. line 1 "An in-memory retry queue with exponential backoff scheduling." then blank line 2; line 106 "Records a failed attempt and reschedules or drops the task." then blank line 107.

expectations.text: First lines are descriptive ("Schedules...", "Returns..."), not imperative ("Schedule...", "Return...")
next_ready_at documents the -1.0 sentinel meaning (task unknown/not pending)
expectations.evidence: Lines 96-98: "or -1.0 if task_id is not pending (never scheduled, already drained, or dropped after exhausting its attempts)."

expectations.text: mark_failed documents KeyError for unknown task_id (Raises:) and the None return meaning the task was dropped after exhausting attempts
expectations.evidence: Lines 122-123: "Raises:\n    KeyError: If task_id is not currently pending." Lines 119-120: "or None if it exhausted its attempts and was dropped from the queue."

expectations.text: drain_ready is documented with a Yields: section (not Returns:) and mentions that drained tasks are removed from the queue
expectations.evidence: Lines 147-150: "Yields:" with "(task_id, payload) pairs ... Each yielded task is removed from the queue as it is produced." No Returns: section.

expectations.text: schedule's Returns: explains the True/False semantics (False = task_id already pending, call ignored)
expectations.evidence: Lines 79-80: "True if the task was newly scheduled; False if task_id was already pending and the call was a no-op."

expectations.text: Args: sections list each parameter with expected types (code has no annotations) and consistent continuation indentation
expectations.evidence: Continuation indentation is consistent (4-space hang), but types are absent from most entries: line 73 "payload: Arbitrary task data handed back verbatim...", line 75 "now: Timestamp at which the task becomes ready.", line 46 "max_attempts: Maximum number of failures..." — no explicit int/float type; only task_id's "Hashable identifier" (line 71) hints at a type.

expectations.text: No comments that merely restate the code (e.g. '# increment attempts' style)
expectations.evidence: Only two comments, both informative: line 58 "# Maps task_id to a mutable [payload, attempts, ready_at] entry." and line 153 "# Snapshot the keys so deleting entries mid-iteration is safe." — both explain non-obvious rationale/structure.

summary.notes: Detailed, accurate full-tier documentation that satisfies everything except stating explicit parameter types in the Args sections.
